 Mobile Market celebrates third year of operation in Lexington 
 By WKYT News Staff Published : Nov. 4, 2026 at 9:03 PM EST | Updated : 3 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google LEXINGTON, Ky. (WKYT) - The Mobile Market is now in its third year of expanding food access across the city of Lexington.
 It is the result of a partnership formed in 2023 by Kroger, God’s Pantry Food Bank and the Lexington-Fayette Urban County Government.
 The 60-foot trailer functions as a grocery store for neighborhoods without access to a full-service grocery store. Customers can pay using a debit card, a credit card or SNAP/EBT.
 The addition of SNAP/EBT benefits has been a boon for the mobile grocery store.
 “The Mobile Market has realized about $120,000 in total sales across 7,000 transactions thanks to the acceptance of SNAP and EBT benefits,” said John Rupp of God’s Pantry Food Bank. “Only 28.5% of those transactions were paid for these methods.”
 City leaders lauded the program.
 “The Mobile Market is a wonderful resource for so many in our community, supporting healthier lifestyles by helping make fresh food more accessible,” Mayor Linda Gorton said. “In 2026, the Mobile Market has generated more than $117,000 in sales through early October, reflecting the ongoing need for this program in our community.”
